title: Solar Position Calculator: Altitude and Azimuth
description: Get the Sun's altitude and azimuth for any place, date and time with the Solar Position Calculator — the pair every sun tool runs on. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, at solar noon on June 21 the Sun over New York stands at altitude 72.7° in the south — while at 9 a.m. it is lower and east of south, numbers this calculator reports minute by minute.

faq: Solar altitude and azimuth for a place, date and time, from the Sun's declination and the local hour angle — the standard astronomical computation.
Can I use it for panel design?
For planning, layout checks and learning, yes — it matches the algorithms design software uses. Certified yield studies run full weather files on top of the same geometry.
Azimuth measured from north or south?
From north, clockwise, on this site (the modern convention). Some older solar texts measure from south — check before mixing sources.
Why is sunrise not due east?
Only at the equinoxes. Declination swings the rise point along the horizon — 58° in New York's June, 122° in its December (computed on this page).
Within roughly a tenth of a degree for the Sun's centre under the standard algorithm — far tighter than any shadow you will measure.
Near the horizon the atmosphere lifts the Sun's apparent position by about half a degree — sunrise/sunset tools include it; raw position readouts state the geometric value.
